configuration.text: Set visible to present the sheet over the page; the screen shows and hides it. Without visible, the sheet renders in place as a plain surface.
Wire onRequestClose to set visible to false: it reports that people asked to close the sheet (a drag down), and the screen hides it.
By default (fillHeight true) the sheet covers the screen and the field sits at its foot.

from.quote: The default: the sheet covers the screen and the field sits at its foot.

configuration.text: Fit the sheet to short content with fillHeight false; it fills the screen by default.

from.quote: A sheet fills the screen by default; fit it to short content instead.

configuration.text: A fitted sheet hugs its content and docks to the bottom.

from.quote: The sheet hugs its content and docks to the bottom.

configuration.text: Do not fill the screen for one line: the sheet covers the page and leaves it empty.

from.quote: The sheet covers the page and leaves it empty.

configuration.text: A scrim (showOverlay) dims the page around a fitted sheet.

from.quote: A scrim dims the page around a fitted sheet

configuration.text: Without a scrim, the page stays bright behind the sheet, as in the Storybook story.

from.quote: The page stays bright behind the sheet, as in the Storybook story.

configuration.text: With showOverlay, set onOverlayPress to hide the sheet when the scrim is pressed; when it's omitted, the scrim calls onRequestClose.
A top inset (topInset) lets the page peek above the sheet; the sheet shortens to keep its bottom on the screen.

from.quote: The page peeks 40 px above, and the sheet shortens to keep its bottom on the screen.

configuration.text: Page type MainPage (the default) and SubPage both give a white sheet.

from.quote: MainPage, the default used everywhere else here, and SubPage both give a white sheet.

configuration.text: Page type JioPlus gives a light grey sheet; its text stays dark, and the HelloJioInput turns white to stand out.

from.quote: A light grey sheet. Its text stays dark, and the HelloJio field turns white to stand out.

configuration.text: Put the AppBar and the HelloJioInput straight in the slot (or in a fragment), not inside a component of your own: the sheet adjusts only the children it can see, so under Page type JioPlus a nested AppBar shows white on the grey sheet and a nested field's pill matches the sheet.

from.quote: The sheet does this only for children it can see: its direct slot children, fragments, and their `children` props.

configuration.text: Turning drag to close off (enableDismissGesture false) means a drag down does nothing, so a stray drag can't lose a half-typed question; the X and the scrim still close the sheet.

from.quote: A drag down does nothing; the X and the scrim still close it, so a stray drag can’t lose a half-typed question.

examples.purpose: Asking a question from Home: the sheet fills the screen over a dimmed page, with an AppBar holding a named close IconButton, one line of Text and a HelloJioInput at its foot. The screen sets visible, and hides the sheet when a question is sent, the X or the scrim is pressed, or a drag asks to close it.

</ModalSheet>

props.name: children
props.description: The sheet adjusts only the slot children it can see: its direct children, fragments, and their children props. An AppBar or HelloJioInput rendered inside a consumer's own component isn't recognised. Declared: Sheet content. Figma exposes one slot — children fill it inside the token-driven padding.

props.name: modes
props.description: The sheet passes its modes to its slot children without Page type (an AppBar keeps it) and without Color Mode Dark; a child's own modes are merged over them. Declared: Design-token modes. Cascaded to every slot child via {@link cloneChildrenWithModes}. `Page type` drives `modalSheet/bg` (`JioPlus` → grey surface).

props.name: fillHeight
props.description: Fill the parent's available height (`flex: 1`). Default `true`. Set `false` to size to slot content. Default true, from the component source.

props.name: visible
props.description: With visible set, the sheet fills its nearest positioned parent as an overlay, and visible false keeps it mounted below the screen. It is not a Modal or portal: the screen sets visible to false on every close. Declared: When set, presents as an animated modal over the page (slide up / down). Omit for a plain in-flow Figma surface (container + slot only).

props.name: showOverlay
props.description: Optional dimming scrim behind the sheet (`overlay/background` token). Presentation mode only. Defaults to `false` (page-sheet peek stays clear). Set `true` for a classic dimmed backdrop; pair with `onOverlayPress` to dismiss. Default false, from the component source.

props.name: onOverlayPress
props.description: Scrim press — typically set `visible` to `false`. Only used when `showOverlay`. When omitted, the scrim calls `onRequestClose` if that is set, so a dimmed sheet can dismiss from the backdrop without a second handler.

props.name: dismissAccessibilityLabel
props.description: Accessible name for the scrim. Defaults to "Dismiss overlay". On the web the scrim is not a tab stop (pointer dismiss still works). Default "Dismiss overlay", from the component source.

props.name: trapFocus
props.description: With trapFocus false, Escape doesn't close the sheet, and a sheet shown from the first render leaves focus on the page; with the default, a sheet shown at load still takes focus. Declared: When `true` (default), opening moves focus to a control inside the dialog and keeps Tab there. Set `false` to render the sheet in a frame or preview without a page-wide trap. Default true, from the component source.

props.name: onRequestClose
props.description: User requested close via swipe-down. Wire to set `visible={false}` (same role as RN `Modal`'s `onRequestClose`).

props.name: enableDismissGesture
props.description: Gates only the drag and its “Drag down to dismiss” hint; the scrim and a close button in the slot still work. Declared: Drag down to dismiss (iOS & Android via `PanResponder`). Presentation mode only. Defaults to `true`. No grabber chrome — Figma has none. Default true, from the component source.

props.name: onDismissed
props.description: Fired after the dismiss slide-down animation completes.

props.name: topInset
props.description: With fillHeight false the sheet docks to the bottom and ignores the inset; with fillHeight it shortens by the inset so its bottom stays on the screen. Declared: Top gap (px) so the layer under the modal peeks above the sheet (iOS page-sheet / card stack). Presentation mode only. Defaults to `40` on iOS and `0` elsewhere.

props.name: presentationProgress
props.description: Optional shared progress `0 → 1` (closed → open), updated during present, dismiss, and swipe. Drive a page-recede (scale / radius / dim) from this so the under-layer stays in sync while dragging.

props.name: style
props.description: Optional style override on the Figma container.

props.name: ...Omit<ViewProps, 'style' | 'children'>
props.description: Inherited React Native props the component also accepts. They are not part of the design contract and no guide documents them.

props.name: accessibilityLabel
props.description: Names the dialog; without it, a slot child's title names it.

modes.name: Page type
modes.description: MainPage and SubPage give a white sheet (#ffffff), JioPlus a light grey one (#f5f5f5). Declared: A token collection ModalSheet reads (the package's FIGMA_COMPONENT_MODES). When modes leave it unset, the resolver uses the collection's default mode.

slots.name: children
slots.description: Sheet content. Figma exposes one slot — children fill it inside the token-driven padding.

events.name: onOverlayPress
events.description: Scrim press — typically set `visible` to `false`. Only used when `showOverlay`. When omitted, the scrim calls `onRequestClose` if that is set, so a dimmed sheet can dismiss from the backdrop without a second handler.

events.name: onRequestClose
events.description: User requested close via swipe-down. Wire to set `visible={false}` (same role as RN `Modal`'s `onRequestClose`).

events.name: onDismissed
events.description: Fired after the dismiss slide-down animation completes.

gaps.text: Under Page type JioPlus, an AppBar or HelloJioInput rendered inside a consumer's own component in the slot isn't recognised: the AppBar loses Page type (white on the grey sheet) and the field's pill isn't repainted, so it still matches the sheet. The #255 fix doesn't reach them; the evidence leaves this limit for Marcin to judge.
A hidden sheet sets inert as the string "true", so React 19 logs a development warning; the sheet still works (#417, Component Bug, To do).
The “Drag down to dismiss” hint has no web mapping, so it isn't exposed on the web.
